cites.quote: began legally mandated meetings with the 10 parties elected to the new Knesset.

notes: No complete per-faction recommendation record was recovered. Hadashot (30 June and 1 July 1992) reports each list’s meeting except Labour’s: Likud for Shamir; Meretz and Tsomet for Rabin; Hadash and the Arab Democratic Party for Rabin on conditions; the National Religious Party, United Torah Judaism and Moledet naming no one. One newspaper each, except Meretz (with Amigoe) and Tsomet (with Amigoe and the Israel Democracy Institute). Labour stays unknown: no report read names its recommendation.

Shas is disputed: Hadashot says it recommended no one, Amigoe that it approved a Rabin-led government. Herzog’s memorandum as quoted later by Amir Oren (Walla, October 2019) says the religious parties left the decision to him and gives 69 for Rabin, 32 for Shamir and three for no one. Labour 44, Meretz 12, Tsomet 8, Hadash 3 and the Arab Democratic Party 2 make 69 without Shas. That fits Hadashot, but it is a check of consistency, not proof of what any single list said.
A 61-seat blocking bloc is not a recommendation tally. Unknown is not an explicit decision to recommend nobody.
